episode_summary: Hashing It Out interview with Pol Lanski of DAppNode on Smooth, a MEV smoothing pool that pools execution-layer rewards so solo stakers get closer to the average payout, covering lottery blocks, MEV, the decentralisation case for home staking, and how the smoothing pool's cheat detection and rewards work.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said he got into crypto in 2014 after Spain's financial crisis taught him that political sovereignty needs economic sovereignty.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: And I got into crypto back in 2014

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said that in 2014, after realising he was late to mining Bitcoin, he started mining Dogecoin.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: So I just started mining Dogecoin.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said he lost the wallet holding his Dogecoin, which became valuable after Elon Musk pumped the coin.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: and then i discovered that i had lost that wallet

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said he had been working with DAppNode since 2019 and had taken over leading the project a couple of years earlier.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: all along since 2019, I have been working with DAPNode.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said DAppNode's biggest use case is people running validators on Ethereum, Gnosis Chain, Lukso and Avalanche.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: That's I would say the biggest use case for DAPNode is people running validators.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said there have been Ethereum lottery blocks worth 400 and 500 ETH.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: there's been blocks with 400 and 500 E.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said most Ethereum lottery blocks are between 0.001 and 0.08 ETH.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: most of the blogs are between 0.001 and 0.08 or something like this.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said lottery blocks above 500 ETH are an anomaly, occurring around 0.01% of the time for much smaller amounts.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: like on the likes of like 0.01% and that's for a lot less than 500 E.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said with around one million Ethereum validators a solo staker can expect about two and a half block proposals per year.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: Now that we have around one million validators, it's basically like two and a half blocks per year that you're expecting.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said fees were very low for a couple of months in 2024 because activity had moved to layer twos.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: seems that all of the activity has moved to layer twos

cards.claim: Pol Lanski compared MEV to Robin Hood selling order flow to Citadel, which then front-ran customers.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: remember how um robin hood was selling the uh private deal flow from all of those uh execution uh orders to citadel and citadel front ran everybody

cards.claim: Pol Lanski explained that a validator can sell its block to searchers and the premium is shared with the block proposer, builders and wallets.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: that premium is essentially the fees that go to not only the block builders but also to whoever the block proposer is

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said solo Bitcoin miners basically never had a real chance to mine a block, which is why mining pools came into existence.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Solo miners in Bitcoin basically never had a real opportunity to ever mine a block and thus never got anything.

cards.claim: The host said MEV is a centralising force that hurts home stakers and Ethereum as a whole.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: mev is a centralizing force that not only plays against the home staker

cards.claim: Pol Lanski argued that decentralisation is a gradient, and that more independent nodes, locations and client implementations add resilience.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: Decentralization is sort of like a gradient where properties emerge, where desirable properties emerge.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski argued that home staking is the gold standard of decentralisation because every home node sits on a different IP address.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: then home staking is the absolute gold standard of the decentralization because every node is in a different IP.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said it should outrage people that centralised players get paid more than home stakers because of uneven MEV distribution.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: centralized players get paid more because of this mev unequal distribution

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said subscribing to the smoothing pool requires a bond of 0.01 ETH.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: You have to pay a bond of 0.01.

cards.claim: A host read an article saying a solo staker earns about 0.149 ETH per year in execution rewards, versus about 0.281 ETH with Smooth.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: in execution rewards per year you're getting 0.14943 eth

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said the median Smooth block reward was about 0.039 ETH, with an average of about 0.085 ETH.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: the median of all of the blocks in smooth which is a representative section of ethereum is 0.039

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said the oracle that tracks whether validators cheat is currently run by DAppNode.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: this oracle is currently run by dapnode

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said Smooth was not yet compatible with EigenLayer restaking but would be in V2.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: so smooth is not compatible now with Eigenlayer but it will be in V2 and we're already

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said vanilla blocks lower Smooth's rewards because they do not come from MEV builders, so an on-chain vote could remove those validators.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: vanilla blocks that have lower rewards because they don't get blocks from from these MEV builders they actually bring the rewards of the pool down

cards.claim: Pol Lanski suggested a Smooth DAO might come, letting pool participants vote to kick out validators that produce vanilla blocks.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: But it might be a Smooth DAO coming.

cards.claim: Pol Lanski said a validator that keeps its block fees for itself is banned from the smoothing pool and never receives pool rewards.
cards.speaker: Pol Lanski
cards.quote: You will be banned from the pool.

title: Pol Lanski: Dappnode | MEV Smoothing Protocol
